Scope and Verification Method

The verification covered the public production domain and core public routes. The verification includes server-side package/version checks, NGINX configuration validation, public HTTP header checks, and live HTTPS response checks.

  • Production domain tested: https://p2p.iiotsolutions.sa
  • Public IP verified: 145.241.154.18
  • Tested public routes: /, /home, /login, /api/health
  • Application validation scope: backend and frontend input validation hardening, XSS prevention, and safe search handling
  • Verification dates: 15–18 June 2026

Finding 1 — Outdated NGINX Version

Result

Resolved

The production web server was upgraded to nginx/1.30.3. Package policy output confirms the installed NGINX version is 1.30.3 from the nginx.org package repository for Ubuntu Noble on arm64.

Verified version: nginx/1.30.3 Installed package: 1.30.3-1~noble Architecture: arm64

This addresses the prior outdated NGINX 1.24.x finding by moving the production edge to a current upstream NGINX release.

Fix 1 verification — NGINX package version

Package verification confirms the production edge is running nginx/1.30.3.

Finding 2 — Web Server Version / Header Disclosure

Result

Resolved

The public Server response header is no longer present on the tested public routes. Verification checks show a Server header count of zero across the root page, home page, login page, and API health route.

/ Server header count: 0 /home Server header count: 0 /login Server header count: 0 /api/health Server header count: 0

The NGINX configuration also keeps server_tokens off enabled. This prevents detailed version disclosure if a product token is ever emitted by a future configuration change.

Fix 2 configuration verification — server tokens, Server header clearing, and CSP

Configuration verification shows server token suppression, response-header clearing, CSP header injection, and a successful NGINX syntax test.

Fix 2 public verification — Server header removed

Public route checks show the Server response header count is zero on the tested application and API routes.

Finding 3 — Content-Security-Policy Header

Result

Resolved / Present

The public application now returns a Content-Security-Policy header on the tested HTTPS application and API routes. The policy restricts scripts to same-origin, blocks plugin/object execution, limits form submission and base URI behavior, and limits framing to same-origin.

default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; font-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net data:; img-src 'self' data: blob: https:; connect-src 'self' https://p2p.iiotsolutions.sa wss://p2p.iiotsolutions.sa; media-src 'self' blob: https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'

Fix 3 public verification — CSP header present

Public route checks show Content-Security-Policy is present on the tested application and API routes.

Finding 4 — Application Form and Input Validation

Result

Resolved

Application-layer input validation and XSS hardening have been added across the relevant backend schemas, API endpoints, and frontend form/popup rendering paths. The completed work addresses the prior concern that application forms accepted suspicious or meaningless values.

Fix 4.1 — Central backend safe-text validation

User-controlled text now passes through validation that rejects dangerous patterns such as script tags, javascript: payloads, path traversal, null bytes, scanner strings, excessive symbols, repeated-character junk, and meaningless values.

Fix 4.2 — Profile and dashboard input validation

Profile names, job title/location fields, expertise tags, dashboard draft fields, post type, category, and related user-editable fields are constrained by validation rules and allowlists.

Profile edit validation

The profile form blocks invalid name characters, HTML-like location input, and invalid expertise tag values before saving.

Fix 4.3 — Forum form validation

Forum post titles, content, tags, category values, replies, and query parameters are validated with length limits, allowed categories/sort values, safe text checks, and strict pagination bounds.

Forum post title HTML validation

The forum post form rejects HTML tag input in the title field and shows a clear validation message.

Forum attachment type validation

The forum attachment flow rejects unsupported file types while showing the allowed image/video formats.

Fix 4.4 — Use-case submission and draft validation

Use-case submission fields and draft payloads enforce safe text validation, valid categories, safe nested values, bounded list sizes, and protection against unsafe payloads while preserving legitimate draft auto-save behavior.

Use-case title special-character validation

The Submit Story form rejects symbol-heavy input in the use-case title field.

Use-case URL and repeated-character validation

The Submit Story form blocks URLs in restricted fields and flags repeated-character junk input in the summary field.

Fix 4.5 — Nested architecture, search, uploads, and frontend XSS prevention

  • Nested technical architecture fields: security_measures and scalability_design are now validated item-by-item so XSS/security payloads cannot bypass checks through nested arrays.
  • Search endpoint hardening: search accepts short legitimate manufacturing terms such as AI, rejects URLs/security payloads, and escapes user text before building MongoDB regular expressions. This prevents regex-style input such as abc.* from becoming an unintended broad regex query.
  • Upload metadata: client-provided file names and upload metadata are checked before persistence so unsafe strings cannot be stored through upload flows.
  • Form-side validation: frontend validation blocks obvious dangerous patterns, URLs in fields where links are not allowed, excessive special characters, repeated characters, and meaningless strings before submission.
  • Backend/frontend consistency: the frontend consecutive-consonant rule was aligned with backend behavior so legitimate manufacturing text is not rejected too aggressively by the browser before the backend can validate it.
  • Map popup XSS prevention: Leaflet popup HTML now escapes user-controlled values before injecting them into raw HTML strings, preventing malicious values from breaking out of attributes or injecting scriptable content.

Conclusion

The reviewed issues have been addressed on the production PeerLink/P2P application and web edge:

  • NGINX has been upgraded to 1.30.3.
  • The public Server response header is absent on tested routes.
  • The public Content-Security-Policy header is present and includes appropriate baseline protections.
  • Application forms and API inputs have been hardened with validation controls for profile, forum, use-case, upload, search, and frontend rendering paths.
